questions.question: What do double solid yellow centerlines mean?

options.text: You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you to drive carefully because the road may become wet and slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that an intersection is coming up. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak can let dangerous fumes into the car. Fix any exhaust system leaks right away.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. Always give a motorcycle the full width of a lane. The rider needs space to move safely.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and cannot see clearly. You should:

options.text: Speed up once the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes clearly before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to signal you to go.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes clearly before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line means you can pass if the way is clear. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To prevent being hit from behind, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic to increase the gap behind you.
Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic to have better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of traffic around you, following the speed limit. This keeps traffic flowing smoothly and helps prevent rear-end crashes.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed. This helps other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians understand what you are doing.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcoholic drink in any part of the vehicle where passengers sit.

questions.question: A train has just passed at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Look and listen for another train. Cross only if the tracks are clear.
Assume no other trains are coming.
Quickly start to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen for another train. Cross only if the tracks are clear.
questions.explanation: After the last car passes, check for trains coming from either direction on any track. Only cross when you are sure the tracks are completely clear.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.
questions.explanation: Use both emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This makes sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: You miss your destination in heavy city traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Back up to where you should have stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive around the block.
questions.explanation: Circle around the block to get back to your destination. Never make a U-turn in heavy traffic as it disrupts other drivers.

questions.question: You cannot drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe for the situation.
A speed that is safe for current road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must follow the speed limit and drive at a safe speed for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. All three limits apply.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Passing is illegal and unsafe on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: When a green light appears, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but first yield to any pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.

questions.question: What can you do to safely drive after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Wait for the alcohol to leave your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the alcohol to leave your body.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, fresh air, food, and showers may wake you up, but they do not make you sober.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your judgment of speed and distance becomes worse.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, worsens vision, distorts judgment of speed and distance, and reduces inhibitions. It does not help you calm down or concentrate.
